subject: math
title: Grade 1 Coins and Money
seo_title: Grade 1 Coins and Money Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Financial literacy – values of coins, and monetary exchanges
meta_desc: Free Grade 1 math worksheets on Canadian coins for the BC curriculum: name the nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie, learn what each coin is worth, compare values, count nickels by 5s and dimes by 10s, and trade 2 loonies for a toonie. 100 questions with pictures and an answer key.
key_big: Look at the value, not the size of the coin.
key_sub: Nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢, loonie $1, toonie $2. The small dime is worth more than the big nickel. A fair trade has the same value: 2 loonies = 1 toonie.
body_html:
Canadian coins

Each coin has a name and a value. Size does not tell the value. The dime is the smallest coin, but it is worth more than the nickel.

CoinValueLook for
nickel5¢bigger than a dime
dime10¢the smallest coin
quarter25¢bigger than a nickel
loonie$1gold colour, 11 sides
toonie$2silver ring, gold centre

Which is worth more?

Look at the value, not the size. 10¢ is more than 5¢, so a dime is worth more than a nickel.

Count by 5s and 10s

Count nickels by 5s. Count dimes by 10s. Count loonies by 1s and toonies by 2s.

Example

How much are 3 dimes?

Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢.

Answer: 30¢

Trade coins

A fair trade gives the same value. 2 loonies are $2, so they trade for 1 toonie.

Example

A sticker costs 15¢. How many nickels pay for it?

Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢.

Answer: 3 nickels

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The dime is small, so it is worth lessLook at the value. The small dime is 10¢. The nickel is 5¢
4 nickels, so 4¢Count the value: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢
More coins is more money3 nickels (15¢) are less than 2 dimes (20¢)
A toonie is $1A loonie is $1. A toonie is $2

faq.q: What do Grade 1 students learn about money in BC?
faq.a: The BC Grade 1 math curriculum includes financial literacy: the values of coins and simple monetary exchanges. Students name the nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie, count coins of one kind, and make trades such as 2 loonies for 1 toonie.

faq.q: Why does my child think a nickel is worth more than a dime?
faq.a: The nickel is bigger, so it looks like more. Put a dime next to two nickels and say “10¢ is the same as 5¢ and 5¢.” Size does not tell the value.

faq.q: How can I help my child learn Canadian coins at home?
faq.a: Use real coins. Sort them, say each name and value, then count nickels by 5s and dimes by 10s. Play store and trade coins, like 2 loonies for a toonie.

faq.q: Do Grade 1 students learn about pennies?
faq.a: No. Canada stopped giving out pennies in 2013, so the nickel is the coin with the least value. Grade 1 uses the nickel, dime, quarter, loonie and toonie.

items.q: What is this coin called?
items.e: This is a nickel. It is worth 5¢.

items.q: What is this coin called?
items.e: This is a dime. It is worth 10¢. It is the smallest coin.

items.q: What is this coin called?
items.e: This is a quarter. It is worth 25¢.

items.q: What is this coin called?
items.e: This is a loonie. It is gold in colour. It is worth $1.

items.q: What is this coin called?
items.e: This is a toonie. It has a gold centre. It is worth $2.

items.q: Which one is the nickel?
items.e: The nickel is worth 5¢. It is A. The dime is smaller, but it is 10¢.

items.q: Which one is the dime?
items.e: The dime is worth 10¢. It is B. It is the smallest coin.

items.q: Which one is the quarter?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. It is B.

items.q: Which one is the loonie?
items.e: The loonie is worth $1. It has 11 sides. It is D.

items.q: Which one is the toonie?
items.e: The toonie is worth $2. It is D.

items.q: Which coin has 11 sides?
items.e: The loonie has 11 sides. It is gold in colour.

items.q: Which coin has a gold centre?
items.e: The toonie has a silver ring and a gold centre. The loonie is all gold.

items.q: Which coin is all gold in colour?
items.e: The loonie is all gold in colour. The toonie is only gold in the centre.

items.q: Which coin is the smallest?
items.e: The dime is the smallest coin. It is worth 10¢.

items.q: Which coin is the biggest?
items.e: The toonie is the biggest coin. It is worth $2.

items.q: What is the name of the $1 coin?
items.e: The $1 coin is the loonie. The $2 coin is the toonie.

items.q: What is the name of the $2 coin?
items.e: The $2 coin is the toonie. “Two” and “toonie” sound alike.

items.q: What is the name of the 25¢ coin?
items.e: The 25¢ coin is the quarter.

items.q: What is the name of the 10¢ coin?
items.e: The 10¢ coin is the dime. The nickel is bigger, but it is only 5¢.

items.q: What is the name of the 5¢ coin?
items.e: The 5¢ coin is the nickel.

items.q: How much is a nickel worth?
items.e: A nickel is worth 5¢. It is bigger than a dime, but worth less.

items.q: How much is a dime worth?
items.e: A dime is worth 10¢. It is small, but it is worth more than a nickel.

items.q: How much is a quarter worth?
items.e: A quarter is worth 25¢, not 20¢.

items.q: How much is a loonie worth?
items.e: A loonie is worth $1. The toonie is $2.

items.q: How much is a toonie worth?
items.e: A toonie is worth $2. The loonie is $1.

items.q: Which coin is worth 5¢?
items.e: The nickel is worth 5¢. It is B.

items.q: Which coin is worth 10¢?
items.e: The dime is worth 10¢. It is B. Small, but worth more than a nickel.

items.q: Which coin is worth 25¢?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. It is B.

items.q: Which coin is worth $1?
items.e: The loonie is worth $1. It is A.

items.q: Which coin is worth $2?
items.e: The toonie is worth $2. It is D.

items.q: How do we write the value of a dime?
items.e: A dime is ten cents. We write 10¢. $10 is ten dollars, much more.

items.q: How do we write the value of a quarter?
items.e: A quarter is twenty-five cents. Cents use the ¢ sign after the number: 25¢.

items.q: How do we write the value of a loonie?
items.e: A loonie is one dollar. Dollars use the $ sign in front: $1. 1¢ is only one cent.

items.q: How do we write the value of a toonie?
items.e: A toonie is two dollars. We write $2. 2¢ is two cents, much less.

items.q: The dime is small. How much is it worth?
items.e: Size does not tell the value. The small dime is worth 10¢. The bigger nickel is 5¢.

items.q: Which coin is worth 25¢?
items.e: The quarter is worth 25¢. The nickel is worth 5¢.

items.q: Which coin is worth less than a dime?
items.e: A dime is 10¢. The nickel is 5¢. 5¢ is less than 10¢.

items.q: Which coin is worth more than a loonie?
items.e: A loonie is $1. The toonie is $2. $2 is more than $1.

items.q: Which two coins are worth dollars?
items.e: The loonie is $1 and the toonie is $2. The nickel and dime are worth cents.

items.q: Which list goes from least to most?
items.e: Nickel 5¢, dime 10¢, quarter 25¢. So nickel, dime, quarter. Do not order by size.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The nickel is 5¢. The dime is 10¢. So the dime is worth more. The nickel is bigger, but size does not tell the value.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The dime is 10¢. The quarter is 25¢. So the quarter is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The quarter is 25¢. The loonie is $1. So the loonie is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The loonie is $1. The toonie is $2. So the toonie is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The dime is 10¢. The nickel is 5¢. So the nickel is worth less. The nickel is bigger, but size does not tell the value.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The quarter is 25¢. The nickel is 5¢. So the nickel is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The loonie is $1. The dime is 10¢. So the dime is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The toonie is $2. The quarter is 25¢. So the quarter is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth more?
items.e: The nickel is 5¢. The loonie is $1. So the loonie is worth more.

items.q: Which is worth less?
items.e: The toonie is $2. The dime is 10¢. So the dime is worth less.

items.q: Which is worth the most?
items.e: Loonie $1, quarter 25¢, dime 10¢, nickel 5¢. The loonie is worth the most.

items.q: Which is worth the least?
items.e: Toonie $2, quarter 25¢, dime 10¢, nickel 5¢. The nickel is worth the least.

items.q: Which is worth the least?
items.e: Toonie $2, loonie $1, quarter 25¢, dime 10¢. The dime is worth the least.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 2 nickels: 10¢. 1 dime: 10¢. They are worth the same.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 3 nickels: 15¢. 1 dime: 10¢. So the 3 nickels are worth more.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 3 dimes: 30¢. 1 quarter: 25¢. So the 3 dimes are worth more.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 1 quarter: 25¢. 4 nickels: 20¢. So the quarter is worth more. More coins is not always more money.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 3 loonies: $3. 1 toonie: $2. So the 3 loonies are worth more.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 4 dimes: 40¢. 1 loonie: $1. So the loonie is worth more. More coins is not always more money.

items.q: Which side is worth more?
items.e: 1 toonie: $2. 2 loonies: $2. They are worth the same.

items.q: Count by 5s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢. That is 10¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 20¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: Count by 10s. How much money is this?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢. That is 20¢. 2¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 10¢ counts dimes by 5s.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢. That is 15¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 30¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: Noah finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. 3¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 15¢ counts dimes by 5s.

items.q: Emma puts these coins in a piggy bank. How much is in it?
items.e: Each loonie is $1. Count by 1s: $1, $2, $3. That is $3. A loonie is $1, not 1¢. $6 counts by 2s, like toonies.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each toonie is $2. Count by 2s: $2, $4. That is $4. $2 counts the coins. A toonie is $2, not $1.

items.q: Mei has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢. That is 20¢. 4¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 40¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. That is 40¢. 4¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 20¢ counts dimes by 5s.

items.q: Wei finds these coins in his pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each loonie is $1. Count by 1s: $1, $2, $3, $4. That is $4. A loonie is $1, not 1¢. $8 counts by 2s, like toonies.

items.q: Arjun puts these coins in a piggy bank. How much is in it?
items.e: Each toonie is $2. Count by 2s: $2, $4, $6. That is $6. $3 counts the coins. A toonie is $2, not $1.

items.q: How much money is this?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢. That is 25¢. 5¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 50¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: Sofia has these coins. How much does she have?
items.e: Each dime is 10¢. Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢, 50¢. That is 50¢. 5¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 25¢ counts dimes by 5s.

items.q: What is the total?
items.e: Each loonie is $1. Count by 1s: $1, $2, $3, $4, $5. That is $5. A loonie is $1, not 1¢. $10 counts by 2s, like toonies.

items.q: Zara finds these coins in her pocket. How much is it?
items.e: Each toonie is $2. Count by 2s: $2, $4, $6, $8. That is $8. $4 counts the coins. A toonie is $2, not $1.

items.q: Ava puts these coins in a piggy bank. How much is in it?
items.e: Each nickel is 5¢. Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢, 25¢, 30¢. That is 30¢. 6¢ counts the coins, not the cents. 60¢ counts nickels by 10s.

items.q: Count the nickels by 5s. What is the next number?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢. 16¢ counts by 1s.

items.q: Count the dimes by 10s. What is the next number?
Count the toonies by 2s. What is the next number?
items.e: Count by 2s: $2, $4, $6, $8. $7 counts by 1s.

items.q: An eraser costs 20¢. How many nickels make 20¢?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢, 20¢. That is 4 nickels. 2 would be dimes.

items.q: A pencil costs 40¢. How many dimes make 40¢?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. That is 4 dimes. 8 would be nickels.

items.q: Chloe trades 2 loonies for 1 coin. It is worth the same. Which coin?
items.e: $1 + $1 = $2. One toonie is $2. 2 loonies = 1 toonie.

items.q: Olivia trades 1 dime for nickels. How many nickels does she get?
items.e: A dime is 10¢. Nickels: 5¢, 10¢. That is 2 nickels. 1 nickel is only 5¢.

items.q: Kai trades 1 toonie for loonies. How many loonies does he get?
items.e: A toonie is $2. Loonies: $1, $2. That is 2 loonies. 1 loonie is only $1.

items.q: 5 nickels are worth the same as 1 ____.
Jasleen trades 2 toonies for loonies. How many loonies?
items.e: 2 toonies: $2, $4. Loonies: $1, $2, $3, $4. That is 4 loonies. 2 loonies is only $2.

items.q: Owen trades 2 nickels for 1 dime. Is it fair?
items.e: 5¢ + 5¢ = 10¢. A dime is 10¢. Yes, it is fair. Size and number of coins do not tell the value.

items.q: Hana trades 1 nickel for 1 dime. Is it fair?
c: Yes, it is 1 coin for 1 coin.
No, the nickel is worth more.
items.e: A nickel is 5¢. A dime is 10¢. No, it is not fair. 1 coin for 1 coin is not always the same value.

items.q: A pencil at the school store costs 10¢. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A dime is 10¢. It is C.

items.q: A sticker costs 5¢. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A nickel is 5¢. It is A. The dime is smaller, but it is 10¢.

items.q: A cookie at the bake sale costs 25¢. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A quarter is 25¢. It is B.

items.q: A juice box costs $2. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A toonie is $2. It is D. A loonie is only $1.

items.q: A peach at the Kelowna farmers' market costs $1. Which coin pays exactly?
items.e: A loonie is $1. It is D.

items.q: Hot chocolate costs $3. Ethan has these coins. Is it enough?
items.e: Toonie $2, loonie $1: $2, $3. Ethan has $3, so yes. $2 comes from counting the toonie as $1.

items.q: A granola bar costs $2. Nadia has 1 loonie. Is it enough?
items.e: A loonie is $1. The bar is $2. $1 + $1 = $2, so she needs $1 more.

items.q: Leah has 3 loonies. She buys a $2 freezie. How much is left?
items.e: 3 loonies are $3. Take away $2: $3 − $2 = $1. $5 adds instead of taking away.

items.q: For the Terry Fox Run, Simran gives 3 toonies. How much is that?
items.e: Count by 2s: $2, $4, $6. That is $6. $3 counts each toonie as $1.

items.q: Noah has 4 dimes. He buys a 10¢ pencil. How much is left?
items.e: 4 dimes: 10¢, 20¢, 30¢, 40¢. Take away 10¢: 40¢ − 10¢ = 30¢. 50¢ adds a dime instead.

items.q: Emma pays for this sticker with nickels. How many nickels?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5¢, 10¢, 15¢. That is 3 nickels. 15 counts the cents, not the coins.

items.q: Lucas pays for this bookmark with dimes. How many dimes?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10¢, 20¢. That is 2 dimes. 4 would be nickels.

items.q: Who has more money?
items.e: Mei has 10¢, 20¢. Mateo has 5¢, 10¢, 15¢. 20¢ is more, so Mei has more. More coins is not always more money.
